output.name: Skelra

anatomy.part: tip of the left tine of the split blade
tip of the right tine of the split blade
the wet-hide binding, a wrap ring round the shaft where it cracked
left end of the T-handle crossbar on the grip
right end of the T-handle crossbar on the grip
splash thrown up by the left stroke, droplets fanning up and left
splash thrown up by the right stroke, droplets fanning up and right

output.myth: On the midsummer crossing Aun was rowing the long boat with his sister's son when Tavo came down off the north like a dropped sail and set his shoulder to the water. The oar that had carried them all summer cracked clean along the grain. Aun wept and cursed and kept rowing with the half of it, because that is what Aun does. When they came in, Ennu the Kite-Wright sat by the fire and bound the crack with wet hide, the way you bind a split finger, and said the hide would shrink tight and hold better than wood. It did. The Split Oar was hung on the Lamp Road that night, and it still rows there, the two tines dipping into the dark whenever the sky goes quiet. Sil looks down from her drowned lamp and says the oar is still rowing toward Aun, who is somewhere in the dark with the boat. Mind your oars in the frost, child. Hide does not forgive.
output.verse:
Two tines dip the dark
the cracked oar rows on in frost
wet hide binds it tight

problems: The blind guess (a stick figure with outstretched arms) doesn't identify an oar. The outline reads as a tall wand or stem, and the splashes read as arms, so the subject is not recognisable as a split oar.
The split blade is not legible. The two tines form a narrow closed triangle with tips at 4906 (~234,107) and 3786 (~303,114), so it looks like a pointed spike rather than a paddle blade with a slit.
The wet-hide binding 4147 (~285,284) sits at the midpoint of a thin line, so it doesn't read as a wrap ring around a shaft.
The T-handle crossbar is nearly collapsed. Its ends 3909 (~296,471) and 3455 (~326,471) are only about 30px apart, and their labels overlap into an unreadable jumble.
The splashes 6061 (~162,191) and 2762 (~370,330) sit mid-figure at roughly binding height, so they look like outstretched arms rather than spray thrown up from the blade strokes.
The figure is drawn as doubled gold and blue strokes running parallel, not as a filled silhouette. It reads as a wireframe rather than a real shape.
The figure is right way up, with the blade at top and the handle at bottom, and the stars are broadly on the intended parts.
